method: One minimal session per runtime with this plugin loaded, one shell command and one reply. An event counts as delivered only when the probe wrote a line for it, and injected context counts as delivered only when the run's random token appears in the model's own reply. Each runtime was measured in its own invocation, so each carries its own token.
instrument_note: An earlier run the same day probed three events. It was widened to five after a census found that the marketplace registers PreToolUse in three plugins and UserPromptSubmit in one, so four of the seven hook-bearing plugins sat outside the instrument that several of their designs named as a release condition.

rows.note: hook trust bypassed for this measurement

blocking.method: A separate session per runtime, in its own working directory. The model is asked to run two commands that each write a file: one allowed, one carrying a token the probe refuses. The evidence is which files exist afterwards, not the model's account of what happened. The allowed command is the control: without it, a missing file would equally mean the refusal held or the model never tried.

rows.note: hook trust bypassed for this measurement

blocking.scope: This establishes that the runtime stops the tool, on Bash, when the hook returns a deny. The prompt instructed the model to accept a refusal rather than retry or route around it, so it does not establish that a model which wants to proceed cannot reach the same result another way.

differences: CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR is set under Claude Code and not under Codex CLI. Everything else measured the same on both, in both modes.
not_measured: Whether a refusal holds for tools other than Bash. The three guards here only claim Bash.
Whether a model told nothing about refusals routes around one. The blocking run instructed the model to accept it, which measures the runtime rather than the model.
Whether a hook can block a Stop, which this probe observes without exercising.
Grok CLI and Gemini CLI, which are recorded in the README as skills-only from a separate reading of their manifests rather than from this probe.
Codex without the hook trust bypass. A runtime that has not been trusted runs no hook at all, so the untrusted state is a configuration answer rather than a contract one.
